segment: Self-hosted running analytics and coaching platforms / running performance analysis software

competitors.name: Strava
competitors.description: Largest social fitness network with activity tracking, segment leaderboards, route discovery, and basic training analytics. Primarily cloud/SaaS, not self-hosted.
strengths: Massive user base (120M+) — strongest network effects in fitness
Segment leaderboards are a unique competitive moat
Best-in-class social features (kudos, comments, challenges)
Strong brand recognition and athlete adoption
Family plan and Strava+Runna bundle for retention
Route discovery and heatmap data are industry-leading
weaknesses: No self-hosted deployment — all data on Strava servers
Limited deep running analytics (no VDOT, no injury prediction)
No daily training recommendations
No shoe tracking or equipment management
Premium required for basic training analysis features
No race prediction based on physiological models
Privacy concerns — data is monetized

pricing.price: $79.99/year ($6.67/mo) or $11.99/mo for Premium; $139.99/yr Family Plan; $149.99/yr Strava+Runna Bundle

competitors.targetAudience: Recreational to serious runners, cyclists, and endurance athletes who value social motivation
competitors.marketShare: Estimated 120M+ registered users; dominant in social fitness tracking

competitors.name: TrainingPeaks
competitors.description: Comprehensive endurance training platform with structured workout planning, coach-athlete management, fitness tracking (PMC), and TrainingPeaks Virtual indoor training.
strengths: Gold standard for coach-athlete workflow
Deep structured workout builder with device sync
Performance Management Chart (PMC) — fitness/fatigue/form
TrainingPeaks Virtual indoor platform
Strength training module with 1000+ video exercises
Used by 87% of WorldTour cycling teams and 40+ national governing bodies
Extensive device ecosystem (Garmin, Wahoo, Zwift, COROS, etc.)
weaknesses: No self-hosted option — proprietary SaaS only
Expensive for individual athletes ($134.99/yr)
No VDOT science or running-specific physiological modeling
No injury prediction or shoe tracking
No route heatmaps or tile exploration
Interface can feel dated and complex
Limited running-specific analytics compared to Hermes

pricing.price: $134.99/year ($11.25/mo) or $19.95/mo Premium; coaching packages from $149/mo (Bronze) to $359/mo (Gold)

features: Strength training with guided video workouts
Device integration (Garmin, Wahoo, Zwift, COROS, etc.)
competitors.targetAudience: Serious endurance athletes and triathletes with coaches; professional cycling teams
competitors.marketShare: Dominant in structured coaching market; 25+ years in market

competitors.name: Runalyze
competitors.description: Manufacturer-independent, privacy-focused running analytics platform with deep physiological metrics (Effective VO2max, training load, race prediction, equipment tracking).
strengths: Privacy-first — German-engineered, data not sold
Effective VO2max calculation — closest competitor to VDOT science
Race prediction with marathon shape calculation
Equipment/shoe tracking with mileage alerts
Performance curves (power, HR, pace) over 90 days
Colored tracks by pace/HR/power on maps
Free tier is very generous
Active development with community feature voting
Manufacturer-independent (syncs Garmin, Suunto, Polar, COROS, etc.)
weaknesses: No self-hosted deployment
No injury prediction
No structured daily training recommendations
No adaptive training plans
No coach-athlete workflow
Premium features (€5.50/mo) are limited compared to Hermes breadth
Smaller community than Strava or TrainingPeaks
features: Colored tracks on map (pace, HR, power, cadence, etc.)
competitors.targetAudience: Data-oriented runners who value privacy, deep analytics, and manufacturer independence
competitors.marketShare: Niche but loyal user base; popular in German-speaking markets and privacy-conscious runners

competitors.name: VeloViewer
competitors.description: Premium Strava data visualization and analysis layer offering deep activity analytics, segment analysis, explorer tile challenges, 3D routes, and pro-level tools for cyclists and runners.
strengths: Exceptional data visualization and infographics
Explorer tiles and challenges are unique gamification
Used by UCI WorldTour professional teams
Very affordable pricing (£10-20/yr)
3D route visualization
Segment analysis with detailed leaderboard insights
Activity wheel and year-wrapped summaries
weaknesses: Requires Strava account — not standalone
No self-hosted option
No training plans or workout builder
No VDOT science or physiological modeling
No injury prediction or shoe tracking
No daily training recommendations
Primarily cycling-focused (despite running support)
Limited to data already in Strava
competitors.targetAudience: Cyclists and runners who want deeper Strava data insights and gamified exploration challenges
competitors.marketShare: Niche; popular in cycling community; used by UCI pro teams for WorldTour package

competitors.name: Intervals.icu
competitors.description: Free, open-API training platform for cyclists, runners, and triathletes with automatic interval detection, PMC fitness tracking, power curve analysis, and structured workout builder.
strengths: Free core platform — no paywall for primary features
Exceptional automatic interval detection
Power-based analytics (FTP estimation, power curve, Coggan metrics)
Performance Management Chart (fitness/fatigue/form)
Open API with 250+ third-party integrations
Custom JavaScript extensions for power users
Active community (160,000+ athletes)
Multisport support with separate zones per discipline
Workout builder with ZWO/FIT/ERG import/export
weaknesses: No self-hosted deployment
Primarily cycling-focused (interval detection built for power data)
No VDOT science or running-specific physiological modeling
No injury prediction or shoe tracking
No daily adaptive training recommendations
No race prediction models
No route heatmaps or tile exploration
Supporter ($4/mo) needed for full history import

pricing.price: Free forever; Supporter $4/mo (unlocks full Strava history, advanced features)

features: Device sync (Garmin, Wahoo, Zwift, COROS, 250+ apps)
competitors.targetAudience: Data-driven cyclists, runners, and triathletes who want free, powerful analytics and interval analysis
competitors.marketShare: 160,000+ active athletes; strong in cycling community

competitors.name: Garmin Connect
competitors.description: Free companion platform for Garmin device users offering activity tracking, health monitoring, Garmin Coach adaptive plans, social features, and basic training analysis.
strengths: Free with Garmin device — no subscription required
Deep integration with Garmin hardware ecosystem
Garmin Coach adaptive training plans (5K, 10K, half-marathon)
Comprehensive health metrics (HRV, sleep, stress, Body Battery)
Strong social features (challenges, groups, badges)
Broad activity tracking (100+ sport profiles)
Garmin Pay, music, and smartwatch features
weaknesses: Requires Garmin hardware — not platform-independent
No self-hosted deployment
No VDOT science or detailed running physiology
No injury prediction
No shoe tracking with mileage alerts
No race prediction based on physiological models
Web interface is limited compared to mobile
Data export and portability restrictions
Limited deep analytics compared to Runalyze or Intervals.icu
features: Health monitoring (HRV, sleep, stress, Body Battery)
competitors.targetAudience: Garmin device owners — recreational to serious athletes
competitors.marketShare: Dominant in GPS watch ecosystem; estimated 25M+ active users

competitors.name: COROS App / Training Hub
competitors.description: Free training platform for COROS watch users featuring EvoLab analytics, structured training plans, team management, coach-athlete communication, and workout builder.
strengths: Free with COROS device — no subscription
EvoLab sports science engine (VO2max, training load, recovery)
Web-based Training Hub for deep analysis
Coach-athlete communication and team management
Drag-and-drop workout builder
Push notifications and real-time sync
Rapidly growing user base and hardware market share
weaknesses: Requires COROS hardware — not platform-independent
No self-hosted deployment
No VDOT science (uses EvoLab proprietary metrics)
No injury prediction
No shoe tracking
No route heatmaps or tile exploration
Web platform is newer and less mature than Garmin Connect
Limited third-party ecosystem compared to Garmin
competitors.targetAudience: COROS watch owners — runners, trail runners, cyclists, and outdoor athletes
competitors.marketShare: Fast-growing; significant market share in GPS watches (3rd behind Garmin and Apple)

competitors.name: Stryd
competitors.description: Running power meter hardware with an adaptive training platform that creates personalized daily workouts, race plans, and running health monitoring based on power metrics.
strengths: Gold standard for running power measurement
Adaptive Training generates personalized daily workouts
Power-based race plans (5K to marathon)
Running health metrics (impact loading rate, lower body stress score)
Wind and environmental compensation
Dual-sided footpath metrics with Stryd Duo
Works with any watch (Garmin, COROS, Apple, etc.)
weaknesses: Requires $199+ hardware purchase
No self-hosted deployment
No VDOT science
No injury prediction based on training history
No shoe tracking
No route heatmaps or tile exploration
Membership ($14.99/mo or $129/yr) is required for full adaptive training features on top of hardware
Power metric has learning curve for new users

pricing.price: Stryd 5.0 $199 (or $14.99/mo for 6mo); Stryd Duo pricing higher; Membership $129/yr ($10.75/mo) for adaptive training

features: Running health monitoring (impact loading, stress score)
Training phases (Base, Peak, Test, Recovery, Maintenance)
competitors.targetAudience: Serious runners and competitive athletes focused on power-based training and race optimization
competitors.marketShare: Leading running power meter brand with strong community following

competitors.name: Final Surge
competitors.description: Free training platform for athletes and coaches with workout builder, device sync, HRV readiness, team social walls, and injury tracking.
strengths: Free core athlete tier
Strong coach-athlete workflow (mailbox, workout comments, video attachments)
HRV and morning readiness with phone camera (Athlete Premium)
Team social wall for group motivation
Pain and Injury Report (PAIR) tracking
Device sync (Garmin, Apple Watch, Zwift, TrainerRoad, Stryd, etc.)
Route builder with GPX/TCX import/export
weaknesses: No self-hosted deployment
No VDOT science or running-specific physiological modeling
No adaptive daily training recommendations
No race prediction models
No route heatmaps or tile exploration
Athlete Premium ($6.58/mo) required for HRV/readiness features
Smaller community and less brand recognition

pricing.price: Free (athlete); Athlete Premium $6.58/mo (billed annually); Coach Starter $19/mo (1-5 athletes); Coach Pro $39/mo (up to 100 athletes)

competitors.targetAudience: Coaches and their athletes; school and college teams; runners and triathletes
competitors.marketShare: Niche but established in coaching market; popular with high school and college programs

positioningGaps.gap: No competitor offers self-hosted deployment — all major platforms are SaaS/cloud-only
positioningGaps.hermesAdvantage: Hermes is self-hosted, giving users full data ownership, privacy, and no subscription lock-in. This is a unique differentiator for privacy-conscious athletes, teams, and organizations.

positioningGaps.gap: No competitor offers VDOT science-based daily training recommendations
positioningGaps.hermesAdvantage: Hermes uses VDOT (Daniels' Running Formula) for daily training paces, unlike competitors who use generic HR/power zones or no structured recommendations. This provides scientifically validated training specificity.

positioningGaps.gap: No competitor offers integrated injury prediction based on training load patterns
positioningGaps.hermesAdvantage: Hermes predicts injury risk from training load trends. Runalyze tracks equipment mileage but no injury prediction; Final Surge PAIR is reactive tracking, not predictive. Hermes is uniquely proactive.

positioningGaps.gap: No competitor combines shoe tracking with predictive mileage alerts AND form-based analysis
positioningGaps.hermesAdvantage: Runalyze tracks shoe mileage but lacks proactive alerts. Hermes tracks shoe health with replacement reminders integrated into the training view.

positioningGaps.gap: No competitor offers route heatmaps integrated with training analytics and race prediction
positioningGaps.hermesAdvantage: Strava has heatmaps but no race prediction. Runalyze has race prediction but no integrated heatmaps. Hermes combines route heatmaps, race prediction, and training analytics in one self-hosted platform.

positioningGaps.gap: No competitor offers a private, self-hosted solution for teams and clubs
positioningGaps.hermesAdvantage: Teams and clubs can self-host Hermes for their entire group without per-seat licensing fees or data leaving their control. No competitor offers this.

positioningGaps.gap: No competitor combines all features (VDOT + training recommendations + injury prediction + shoe tracking + heatmaps + race predictions) in one platform
positioningGaps.hermesAdvantage: Athletes currently need 3-4 platforms (e.g., Strava + Runalyze + TrainingPeaks + VeloViewer) to get what Hermes offers in one. Hermes is the only all-in-one running analytics platform.

competitiveThreats.threat: Strava adding deeper running analytics and VDOT-like features via partnerships (e.g., Runna bundle)
Runalyze adding adaptive training plans and injury prediction (natural evolution of their platform)
Intervals.icu expanding running-specific analytics beyond cycling focus
Garmin adding VDOT-like science to Garmin Coach (leveraging Firstbeat analytics they already own)
COROS EvoLab becoming more sophisticated with daily training recommendations
Stryd adding full training load and injury prediction to their adaptive training platform
Self-hosted feature becoming table stakes — competitors offering self-hosted options
Apple Fitness+ or Health app expanding into structured running analytics
